text: MEETING OF OWNERS AND MINERS USELESS.

label: text
text: As the outcome of Mr. Evan Williams's letter to Mr. Herbert Smith a meeting of the coal owners' representatives and the Miners' Federation officials was held this afternoon, lasting three hours and a half, but it was abortive.

label: text
text: The mine owners' statement says that the other side emphasised that they were not disposed to shift from the position they have so far taken up. The owners regretfully conclude that there appears no immediate hope of carrying the matter further.

label: text
text: Reuter "learns that the atmosphere of the conference was far from conducive to peace.

label: text
text: The miners, it is alleged, took up a chafenging, impatient attitude. They absolutely refused to consider a departure from the present hours of working, and would not entethain an eight-hours day under any circumstances or a reduction in wages. They expressed the opinion that a reduction was not necessary if reorganisation of the industry were carried out.

label: text
text: A resume of the conclusions of the Committee that recently met at Geneva to consider the proposed reconstitution of the League Council, and which will provisionally meet again on June 28, was given by Viscount Cecil in the House of Lords.

label: text
text: The stated that it was agreed there would be nine instead of six non-permanent members, who would hold office for three years. One-third would retire annually, while only one might be re-elected, if the Assembly agreed by a two-thirds majority, otherwise those who retired would not again be eligible until three years later. The idea was to be rotation of office to enable members sitting on the Council as non-permanents henceforth to assume office immediately they were elected instead of at the next New Year.

label: text
text: The new scheme would make a Council of fourteen, assuming that Germany came in next September, or sixteen if the United States and Russia entered. Admittedly this was a fairly large number, but he saw no reason why it should not work successfully.

label: text
text: The Committee thought that three non-permanent members should represent the South American States.

label: text
text: The newspaper "Oglobo" announces that Brazil is formally notifying its resignation from the League of Nations in a few weeks time, and will not participate in the Assembly meeting in September at Geneva.

label: text
text: It is noteworthy in connection with this that the Brazilian representative, Senator Franco Mello, was absent at yesterday's meeting of the Council on the ground of indisposition, but failed to send the usual substitute.

label: text
text: The talk of the Brazilian withdrawal from the League causes difficulties in connection with the reconstruction of the League Council. Yesterday's meeting opened with two significant absentees, Senhor Mello and also Senhor Quinones de Leon (Spain) who was suddenly recalled to Spain; though, unlike Senhor Mello, he provided a deputy in the Council.

label: text
text: It is semi-officially explained that Senor, Leon was recalled to exchange views on international policy, not connected with the League, though Senor Yanguus, Foreign Minister, interviewed, pointed out that the feeling of the recent meeting of the Commission examining the Constitution of the Council sided with Lord Cecil's viewed which was contrary to Spanish narrations. Consequently, the present meeting at Geneva is not interesting to Spain, since the presence of all members is not necessary for the functioning of the organisation, but in order to testify her loyalty to the League Spain has appointed her Charge d'Affaires in Berne to sit in Senor Leon's absence.

label: text
text: The session of the Committee on the Composition of the Council has been fixed for June 28. The adjourned extraordinary session of the Council is being convened before the meeting of the Assembly in September. This indicates that no agreement has been reached with Spain and Brazil as regards the future composition of the Council.

text: The Liberal Parliamentary Party split between the Lloyd Georgian and the Oxfordian sections resulted in a meeting in the House of Commons at which 33 were present.

label: text
text: A letter was read from the Earl of Oxford saying that nothing had happened to alter the views he recently expressed criticising Mr. Lloyd George's attitude during the strike.

label: text
text: A motion that the Liberal M.P.'s deprecated the publicity given to the leaders' differences and hoped for the restoration of unity was carried by 20 votes to 10 after an amendment to delete the first part had been rejected by 20 votes to 12.

label: text
text: The voting thus favoured the Lloyd Georgians.

label: text
text: The opinion is expressed that Sir John Simon will lead the Lord Oxford section in the House of Commons.

label: text
text: Their Majesties the King and Queen were present at Covent Garden on the occasion of Dame Meiba's farewell operatic performance. At the head of the main staircase stood a bust of the diva, surrounded by flowers.

label: text
text: Their Majesties congratulated the singer, and wished her every happiness in her retirement.

label: text
text: At the conclusion of the memorable performance the stage was a mass of flowers. The audience was keyed up to the highest pitch of enthusiasm.

label: text
text: Lord Stanley, Chairman of the Royal Colonial Institute, handed her a bouquet and dwelt on the admiration and affection which Dame Melba inspired. He conveyed a message of love from every corner of the Empire.

label: text
text: Dame Melba, much moved, spoke of her grief that never again would she sing in the beloved walls of Covent Garden.

label: text
text: There was tumultuous applaus as Dame Melba repeatedly kissed her hand to the audience, women throwing flowers and bouquets on the stage.

label: text
text: The Japanese destroyer, "No. 14," left to day after having spent two days in and near Canton harbour. The trip up-river was made to rescue a Japanese freighter which had been attacked by pirates.

label: text
text: On June 4, the freighter "Nishi Maru" ran aground on the second bar, below Canton. That night, pirate craft surrounded the steamer, which could not get off the bar. Several unsuccessful assaults mere made by the pirates. On Sunday morning, a Chinese gunboat drew alongside and the pirates dispersed, but when the gunboat left the pirates returned in force and tried repeatedly to board the "Nishi Maru" until the Japanese destroyer steamed around a bend in the stream.

label: text
text: One foray netted the pirates a considerable quantity of Canton-bound freight which had been put on to a lighter.

text: The eighth International Labour Conference closed on June 5. The ninth opened yesterday, and deals with maritime questions.

label: text
text: The Conference debated to-day the drafting of an international code of rules relating to seaman's agreements.

label: text
text: Mr. Cuthbert Laws, the British employers' delegate, reproached the International Labour Office for not applying the decisions of the Genoa Conference.

label: text
text: The Director of the Labour Office replied. He said that the Genom Conference endeavoured to effect a uniform settlement of judicial conditions for seamen, and the Labour Office acted in conformity with the Genoa policy in drawing up a Convention which "the Governments never criticised.

label: text
text: Mr. Henson, the British workers' delegate, opposed the proposals of the employers, which Mr. Cuthbert Lawe submitted, for observance of the international seamen's statute as fixed at Genoa.
